newsitem.title: CHINA: HK property stocks slump on concerns over policy.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks slump on concerns over policy.

text.p: Share prices of major property developers tumbled in Thursday morning trade on worries over potential measures to be unveiled by Hong Kong's new government to curb rising property prices, analysts and brokers said.
But brokers added selling pressure was not great.

Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa hinted on Wednesday that his government would take steps to cool speculation and spiralling prices in the residential property market, but did not specify what measures would be taken.
"His tone was firm and sounded quite decisive. We expect some precise and comprehensive measures to turn up sometimes later," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
Sun Hung Kai Properties slipped to a day's low of HK$89.50, then clawed back some ground to trade HK$2.00 down at HK$91.25.
The share was an institutional portfolio favourite but was also one of the most liquid shares in the market, brokers said.
Henderson Land fell HK$2.50 to HK$66.25, then recovered to trade HK$1.50 lower at HK$67.25 on low turnover.
Cheung Kong, the heaviest traded property stock, slipped HK$1.00 to HK$75.50 on trade of HK$227 million.
New World Development slipped HK$0.50 to HK$45.70, but on very low volume of HK$86.8 million.
Analysts said the company was one of the largest property developors but also had a well diversified earnings base.

"The developers had a private meeting with the new government last Thursday and developers prices were weak last Friday," said Archie Hart associate director in BZW Securities Asia. "Today we are seeing a continuation of that trend."
